page.overview:
What is Walther PPK?

The Walther PPK is a compact semi-automatic pistol that is a iconic staple in all James Bond media, being the titular 00 Agent's go-to sidearm in a sweeping number of stories in the long-running franchise. Produced by Carl Walther GmbH, it is a more compact variant of its larger parent weapon, the [https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Walther_PP Walther PP] (Walther Polizeipistole), originally introduced in 1929. The Walther PPK (the K appendix standing for either Kriminalpolizei or Kurz (short)) itself was introduced in 1931 and temporally ended production in 2025, lasting nearly a century. Due to its success and popularity, the gun model and its shape have been widely copied, even into toy guns. The gun is of high quality, and is therefore considered a quality standard in expert circles.

The Walther PPK is arguably the single most recognizable firearm in the James Bond franchise, becoming as synonymous with the character as the Aston Martin DB5, the martini, or the black tuxedo. Since Ian Fleming first armed Bond with this pistol in Dr. No (1958), it has served as the spy's signature weapon across novels, films, comics, television, and video games since for over six decades.

The decision to replace Bond's earlier Beretta .25 with the Walther PPK followed firearms expert Geoffrey Boothroyd's criticism that the Beretta lacked adequate stopping power. Boothroyd recommended the 7.65 mm Walther PPK, describing it as a compact, reliable pistol suitable for a professional intelligence officer. Fleming incorporated this advice directly into Dr. No, introducing Major Boothroyd—later known to film audiences simply as Q—as the armourer who insists Bond adopt the PPK. This real-world correspondence permanently shaped one of fiction's most iconic weapons.

Although the PPK is modest in size and power compared with many military sidearms, its compact dimensions, concealability, reliability, and understated appearance perfectly embody Bond's role as a covert intelligence operative rather than a front-line soldier. The pistol reflects the series' emphasis on precision, professionalism, and discretion over overwhelming firepower.

Also known as: PPK, Walther.
